readme: Models the suite can be pointed at. `url` accepts a bare /v1 base or a full
chat-completions URL. `contextTokens` is what one request may use, which is
not the backend's total context when it serves parallel slots.
`chatTemplateKwargs` is forwarded verbatim; a reasoning backend needs
{"enable_thinking": false} or it answers into reasoning_content and returns
empty content. `outputHeadroom` is extra output tokens a model needs before
it starts answering: a reasoning backend spends them thinking, and without
it every reply is preamble that ends mid-thought.
Do not hand-write an entry: `run.py add-model --url ... --model ...` reads
contextTokens, expectParams, expectModelPath and sizeGiB off the live
endpoint and probes where the reasoning goes. Then `run.py models` shows
every entry against what each endpoint is serving right now.
`fingerprintUrl` points at somewhere that reports model metadata when the
serving port does not: a proxy answers /v1/models with an id and nothing else,
while the backend it fronts serves the same ids with params, quant, and context.
For a hosted model add "apiKeyEnv": "SOME_ENV_VAR"; the suite reads the key
from the environment and never stores it here.
`tier`, `family`, `sizeGiB` and `coResident` are read by the report only.
`coResident` means the weights fit in the VRAM left over while the bulk tier
is loaded, so this model could serve a stage in parallel rather than instead.

chat-27b.label: Qwen3.6-27B-Q6_K (chat, non-thinking)
chat-27b.notes: The bulk tier every skill uses today. This is the baseline the others are read against. Served by chat-backend-dense across both 3090s; :8004 and :8008 are two request-shaping profiles in front of the same llama-server, so this and think-27b address the same weights. expectModelPath is checkable here only because the stack state API reports the launched path for proxied backends; :8010 itself reports metadata but not launch argv, so on a deployment without that API this claim goes unchecked rather than failing. expectQuant is what separates this from chat-27b-q4, since a requant falls inside the parameter-count tolerance by design.

think-27b.label: Qwen3.6-27B-Q6_K (code, thinking)
think-27b.notes: The verification tier. Same weights as chat-27b with reasoning on, so the gap between the two is the value of thinking rather than of scale. Reasoning consumes the output budget before the answer starts, so every case needs headroom. First set to 3000 from two probe items at ~1,900 tokens; a full run then showed real cases spending 3,500-9,938, truncating items in four of twelve. Raised to cover the observed maximum with margin. A cap costs nothing unless it is reached, so err high: too low silently converts a model failure out of thin air.

task-4b.label: Qwen3.5-4B-UD-Q6_K_XL (task)
task-4b.notes: Fingerprinted 2026-08-03: 4.21B params, Q6_K, 1 slot. contextTokens corrected to 65538 on 2026-08-04 from TASK_CTX_SIZE on the live stack; it had been 32768, which under-budgeted every task-tier prompt by half. Shares a router with embed/ocr/rank at MODEL_ROUTER_MAX=1, so the first call after another member ran pays a swap. chatTemplateKwargs is now redundant here — the router's own preset passes --chat-template-kwargs {"enable_thinking":false} — but it is kept because it costs nothing and survives a preset that stops doing so.

task-9b.label: Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M (task)
task-9b.notes: Fingerprinted 2026-08-05: 9.20B params, Q4_K - Medium, 5.46 GiB, and contextTokens read as 65792 rather than the 65538 the 4B reports — the two task models are not launched identically. **65792 is what it serves beside the 35B-A3B MoE, and is not a property of this model alone.** Those two co-reside comfortably; beside the 27B dense the KV cache does not fit and this model has to be relaunched below 65k. So re-run `add-model --write` after any change to what occupies the primary backend, or every task-tier prompt is budgeted against a ceiling the server no longer has — the same failure that left contextTokens at 32768 for months, in the other direction. Only servable when the router has these weights loaded; :8007 serves whichever task model is configured, so `run` refuses unless the endpoint matches expectModelPath, and task-4b and this entry can never both be runnable. The probe answers in visible content, so no outputHeadroom is needed; chatTemplateKwargs is kept because it costs nothing and survives a router preset that stops passing it. Earlier results under results/task-9b/ predated fingerprinting and could not be attributed, so they were moved to results/_unattributed-task-9b-preflight/ rather than compared against.

moe-35a3b.label: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q6_K (chat, MoE)
moe-35a3b.notes: 35B total, ~3B active. Fingerprinted 2026-08-05: 35.51B params, Q6_K, 27.94 GiB. The entry previously described a Q4_K_M build estimated from the model's name; the weights actually loaded are Q6_K, which is the better comparison — chat-27b is also Q6_K, so the gap between them is architecture (35B-A3B sparse against 27B dense) with quantization held fixed. It is also 6.6 GiB larger than chat-27b rather than smaller. Occupies the same primary-backend slot as chat-27b — `chat-backend-moe` is a variant of the service behind :8004/:8008, not a separate port — so exactly one of this and chat-27b is servable at a time, and loading it takes think-27b down too. The stack reports 255998 context on one slot for this variant; contextTokens is held at 131072 so the long-context rungs measure the same prompt against both.

chat-27b-q4.label: Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M (chat, non-thinking)
chat-27b-q4.notes: The same weights as chat-27b at a smaller quant, so the gap between the two is the cost of quantization alone, with scale and reasoning held fixed. Shares the primary-backend slot with chat-27b and moe-35a3b. Fingerprinted 2026-08-08, when these weights were first loaded: 27.32B params, Q4_K - Medium, 15.92 GiB — 5.38 GiB less than chat-27b's Q6_K, which is the whole reason to consider it. The entry that predated the load guessed a UD-Q4_K_XL build at 16.68 GiB from the name; the file actually loaded is plain Qwen3.6-27B-Q4_K_M.gguf, and the label and size are now the measured ones. expectParams cannot separate it from chat-27b — a requant moves the count by less than the 10% tolerance, which is exactly what that tolerance is for — so expectQuant and expectModelPath are the discriminators, and both are now measured rather than guessed. Note that loading this takes :8008 with it: think-27b's Q6_K results, and the forge_routing rows resting on them, describe weights that are no longer loaded while this is up.

moe-35a3b-think.label: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q6_K (code, thinking, MoE)
moe-35a3b-think.notes: Added 2026-08-05, because loading the MoE takes :8008 with it: the thinking profile a deployment running this variant actually gets is this, not think-27b. That matters more than it looks — `forge/lib/forge_routing.py` sends single-speaker cleanup and braindump splitting to `think`, and both decisions were measured on the 27B. If the MoE stays the primary backend, those two rows rest on weights that are no longer loaded. Same weights as moe-35a3b with reasoning on, so the gap between them is the value of thinking with architecture held fixed, exactly as think-27b is to chat-27b. The probe reasoned 303 tokens against the 27B profile's ~1,900; outputHeadroom is nonetheless held at the 12000 floor measured across a full run, because a one-question probe cannot size a real case and a cap costs nothing unless it is reached.
